newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks dip as investors cash in gains.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks dip as investors cash in gains.

text.p: Caracas stocks slipped on profit-taking as investors cashed in gains after 10 straight record-breaking sessions, traders said.
Despite the dip, the market is poised to return to its upward trend, they said.
"I think investors are just waiting for the adjustment to play itself out before they come back again," said Banesco broker Hugo Ortega.
The bourse's 19-share index closed down 0.87 percent at 6,335.53. Nearly 50 million shares traded worth seven billion bolivars ($15 million).
The session began with a burst as market-leader Electricidad de Caracas jumped 10 bolivars to 610 on confirmation of tariff increases.
"But profit-taking soon dragged down the stock, and indeed the rest of the market," said Ortega.
Electricidad closed off 19 bolivars at 581. Among total traded issues, 23 fell, 15 rose and five closed flat.
"Investors only took profits so that they could come back; this is still a strong market," said one broker.
